landing.catalogText: Open feeds with current service from operators around the world. Pick one and import it to explore it.
landing.filesText: The core GTFS Schedule files are edited and validated field by field. Columns it doesn't know are kept on export.

what.a: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) is the open format transit operators use to publish lines, stops, timetables and calendars. It is a ZIP of text files used by trip planners and mobility apps.

create.q: Can I create a GTFS feed from scratch?
create.a: Yes. Create a blank feed with its agency, add stops, routes and calendars in the editor, and use the generator to create the trips and stop times.

validate.a: GTFS Manager checks the whole feed: required files and fields, references between files, stop times that go backwards or are too fast, stops without coordinates or service, expired calendars and route colour contrast. Each warning links to the affected records.

large.a: Yes. Files are read as a stream and the data is stored in a SQLite database inside your browser. Feeds like Renfe Cercanías, with more than 130,000 trips, are imported and explored in full.

data.a: Only in your browser: feeds are kept in this site's private storage on your device and are never sent to any server. To keep a copy or move them to another device, export them as a GTFS ZIP. Clearing the site's data deletes them.

export.q: Can I export the feed again?
export.a: Yes, at any time. Export builds a GTFS ZIP with every file and keeps the extra columns the original had.
